easy.q: Which commandment was Elder Villanueva's talk mostly about?
options: Keeping the Sabbath day holy
Paying a full tithe
Living the Word of Wisdom
easy.why: Elder Villanueva said that after his family's baptism, the change that took the greatest faith and sacrifice was to pay a full tithe, and he testified of the blessings that follow.

easy.q: When Elder Villanueva was a boy and money was scarce, who in his family chose to trust the Lord's promise about tithing?
options: His mother
His grandfather
His oldest brother
easy.why: His mother was providing for eight children, yet when the missionaries taught the law of tithing she “chose to trust the Lord’s promise” in Malachi.

easy.q: Elder Villanueva invited a sister who was worried about tithing to write something. What was it?
options: A letter to her bishop
A journal of her prayers
A list of her blessings
easy.why: He invited her to write her own list of the blessings the Lord had given her, because such blessings are often easy to overlook.

easy.q: A sister said in sacrament meeting that something in her home lasted far longer than she expected. What was it?
options: A bag of rice
A propane tank
A box of candles
easy.why: Her propane tank seemed as though it would never run out. She knew this was one of the Lord's tender mercies for paying an honorable tithing.

easy.q: In the Bible story Elder Villanueva told, what did Elijah ask the widow of Zarephath to do first?
options: Make him a little cake
Build him a small room
Sell her oil at the market
easy.why: Elijah said, “make me thereof a little cake first.” She did as he asked, and her meal and oil did not run out.

medium.q: What did Elder Villanueva use Doctrine and Covenants 130:20–21 to teach?
options: Blessings come to everyone equally, whatever they choose
Blessings come mostly through many years of Church service
Every blessing from God comes by obeying the law it is based on
The laws that bring blessings change with each generation
medium.why: The verse says that when we obtain any blessing from God, “it is by obedience to that law upon which it is predicated.” Elder Villanueva bore witness of this truth.

medium.q: A sister's testimony of tithing weakened because she never got the promotion she hoped for. Which point of the talk does her story illustrate?
options: We may expect blessings our way instead of in the Lord's way and timing
Tithing brings blessings only when it is paid without any hardship
The Lord's promise in Malachi is about the next life, not this one
Temporal blessings are never among those promised to tithe payers
medium.why: Just before her story, Elder Villanueva said we sometimes expect blessings “the way we would wish, rather than in His own way and timing.”

medium.q: Why did Elder Villanueva quote Elder Bednar's talk “The Windows of Heaven”?
options: To explain how the Church uses the tithing it receives
To show that tithing blessings are often subtle and easy to overlook
To show that tithing blessings usually come as more income
To show that tithing blessings come only to those in great need
medium.why: Elder Bednar taught that we often receive “significant but subtle blessings” that are not what we expect and can easily be overlooked.

medium.q: Elder Villanueva quoted the Lord's words that Israel's clothes and shoes did not wear out in forty years. What question did he then ask us?
options: Whether we give thanks often enough for what we own
Whether we would follow a prophet into the wilderness
Whether we own more possessions than we truly need
Whether the Lord has made our own possessions last longer
medium.why: He asked whether the Lord has caused our personal possessions to last longer because we have faithfully lived the law of tithing.

medium.q: Why does the widow of Zarephath remind Elder Villanueva of his mother?
options: Both were taught by missionaries who came to their homes
Both were given great wealth soon after they obeyed
Both trusted the Lord's promise and gave when they had very little
Both asked for a sign before they were willing to give
medium.why: He thinks of the widow when he remembers his mother's faith in difficult years. Each trusted a promise from the Lord and gave in spite of her circumstances.

hard.q: Elder Villanueva listed blessings such as steady work, good health and gratitude. What did he say these blessings are evidence of?
options: That spiritual blessings matter more than temporal ones
That he had managed his money with unusual care
That blessings arrive soon after each tithing payment
That the Lord has indeed opened the windows of heaven
hard.why: He said these blessings, “both temporal and spiritual,” are evidence that the Lord has opened the windows of heaven and poured out His promised blessings in abundance.

hard.q: Which situation best fits the kind of tithing blessing this talk says is easy to overlook?
options: A family's old car keeps running well year after year
A family receives a large and unexpected inheritance
A worker is promoted the week after paying tithing
A student wins a scholarship in a public ceremony
hard.why: The talk speaks of “significant but subtle blessings” that are not always what we expect, such as possessions that last, rather than dramatic gains.

hard.q: After teaching that every blessing comes by obedience to law, Elder Villanueva quoted the Lord: “Who am I … that have promised and have not fulfilled?” What does this add to his reasoning?
options: That the Lord tells us beforehand when each blessing will come
That the Lord is sure to keep the promise He attaches to a law
That the Lord gives each blessing in the form we have asked for
That the Lord made such promises chiefly to Saints of earlier days
hard.why: The law tells us what to do; this verse assures us the Lord fulfills what He promises. Elder Villanueva then added that we sometimes expect blessings our way “rather than in His own way and timing.”

hard.q: According to Elder Villanueva, what did Elijah understand when he asked the widow to feed him first?
options: That the famine would end within a few days
That the widow had more food than she admitted
That blessings will come after the trial of our faith
That a prophet's needs come before a family's needs
hard.why: Elder Villanueva said, “Elijah understood that blessings will come after the trial of our faith.” The widow offered all she had, and then the promise was fulfilled.

hard.q: In his closing testimony, why did Elder Villanueva say the Lord gives us commandments?
options: Because He wants us to receive His blessings
Because He wants to see how much we will give up
Because sacrifice is meant to be its own reward
Because His Church depends on what we can give
hard.why: He testified, “He gives us commandments because He wants us to receive His blessings.” Tithing is an invitation to be blessed.
